history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG - this CSV row is the same shrine as seq 2114 ('Bisaldeo (Gokarneswar) Temple, Bisalpur'): a 12th-century Shaivite temple dedicated to Gokarneshvara, commissioned by the Chahamana king Vigraharaja IV (Bisal Deo, r. c. 1150-1164 CE), an ASI Monument of National Importance beside the Bisalpur Dam on the Banas River. No separate 'Bisaldeo Temple' exists in Tonk town - every listing (Justdial 'Bisal Dev Mandir, Bisalpur Dam'; Rajasthan tourism) points to the Bisalpur site; CSV town 'Tonk' is the district, not the town. Coordinates copied from seq 2114 (same site). See seq 2114 for the full entry.

name: Bisaldeo Temple (duplicate of seq 2114)
town: Bisalpur (CSV says Tonk; actual site is the village of Bisalpur, Tonk district)
town_description: Bisalpur is a village in Deoli tehsil of Tonk district, Rajasthan, on the Banas River at the Bisalpur Dam (completed 1999), about 150 km from Jaipur. Known for the dam reservoir, the 12th-century Bisaldeo temple and the older Gokarna cave shrine, it is an offbeat heritage and pilgrimage spot.
tradition: Shaivite (Gokarneshvara; ASI-protected monument with living worship)

travel.railway: Tonk has no railway station; nearest major railheads Jaipur (~150 km) and Sawai Madhopur (~120 km, verify)
travel.road: On SH 37A near Bisalpur Dam; ~80 km from Tonk town by road (verify)

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Maha Shivaratri draws thousands. Note the courtyard may be submerged when reservoir levels are high.
visitor_information.opening_hours: ASI monument; typically accessible sunrise-sunset - verify locally
